answer: A berth is held by one bonded keeper, not a stack of names. An agent escrows 38.4 POA for one numbered walnut press at pier 7 of the night wharf and must keep the stones turning through a 6-hour tide. A lot-chosen inspector arrives, cracks a fresh hull against the press, stamps the oil blot onto a numbered slate that also bears that night's painted nebula mark, and demands a signed hash of blot and mark within 21 seconds while the oil is still wet. Remote clones cannot stand at that press or read the wall from a second berth. A dry blot or a late hash slashes 8.6 POA and yields the press.
